note: PASS WITH CAVEATS, five of them, none of which affects the item<->code mapping. (1) LANGUAGE. The children answered a FRENCH child self-report EAS (Gasman et al. 2002, ref [36] of the PLOS paper); the deposit (journal.pone.0276665.s001, a single unlabelled 256x113 RawData sheet whose only text is the column headers) and the paper contain no French item wording, so the translated_substitute fallback applies: English in the base fields, language=French, _translated columns empty. (2) WHOSE ENGLISH. The shipped English is neither Buss & Plomin's own wording nor the study's: it is the English rendering of the 20 EAS items published in IJERPH 2022;19(3):1387 Table 2 (CC BY 4.0), a Mexican study using the Spanish adaptation. It was chosen because it is the only open-access source I found that carries all 20 items in one consistent register with the reversal markers; MoBa (PMC4690074) and PMC4721433 give Buss & Plomin's own English verbatim for only 14 of the 20, and stitching three renderings together would still have left item 16 unsourced. Transcribed verbatim including that table's typo 'When goings from one place to another' (ACT2). Its rendering of item 16 ('Is lonely', SOC4) drifts from the Spanish it translates ('Es algo solitario', i.e. somewhat solitary/a loner) -- flagged in public_note. (3) PERSON. The shipped text is third-person ('Has a tendency to be shy') while the administered form was first-person; the paper's own four English examples read 'I cry easily', 'I run from morning to night', 'I like to be with others', 'I am rather shy'. Four items is not an instrument, so the consistent third-person source was used for all 20 rather than mixing. (4) TWO RESPONSE DIRECTIONS IN ONE TABLE, deliberately. data/gerber_2022_swisscamp.py recodes the six reverse-worded items (ACT2, ACT5, TIM2, TIM3, TIM5, SOC4) as 6 - raw, so for those six the stored resp runs 1=strongly agree .. 5=strongly disagree while the other fourteen run 1=strongly disagree .. 5=strongly agree. The option_text follows the DATA, not the questionnaire. irw-validate may flag resp_ambiguous on this table; that flag is correct and the anchors are still right. (5) resp 2, 3 and 4 ship blank and instructions is blank -- the paper labels only the two endpoints ('from 1 (strongly disagree) to 5 (strongly agree)') and publishes no instruction text. RIGHTS: no restriction found to quote for the EAS; its wording is reproduced in full in a CC BY 4.0 article, so neither 2026-09-04 ruling fires. SOURCES THAT WERE BOT-WALLED: hal.science (Anubis proof-of-work, Rouxel 2013 French EAS), link.springer.com (303 to idp.springer.com; Gasman 2002 and the EASI encyclopedia entry), cataloguementalhealth.ac.uk (403), scribd (403). Any of those, or the Gasman 2002 full text, could supply the administered French and would upgrade this table.
public_note: The children answered a French self-report version of the EAS temperament questionnaire; neither the paper nor its deposit publishes the French wording, so the item text shown here is an English rendering of the same numbered EAS items taken from another study (IJERPH 2022;19(3):1387, Table 2) and is third-person where the children read first-person. Read SOC4 with care: its English here, 'Is lonely', renders an item that in the original describes a child who tends to be solitary. Six items (ACT2, ACT5, TIM2, TIM3, TIM5, SOC4) are stored reverse-recoded in the IRW table, so their response anchors run 1 = strongly agree to 5 = strongly disagree, the opposite direction from the other fourteen.
